text:
**Renting vs. buying: what to weigh**

Whether to rent or buy depends more on how long you will stay than on your beliefs about homeownership.

- **Time horizon:** Buying has closing costs of 2–5% of the purchase price. When you sell, you also pay agent commissions. If you expect to move within about five years, you usually lose money by buying. Early mortgage payments go mostly to interest, so equity builds very slowly at first.
- **Price-to-rent ratio:** A ratio above about 20 favors renting. A ratio below 15 favors buying.
- **Ongoing costs:** First-time buyers often stretch to borrow the largest loan a lender will approve. They then find that owning has its own costs. Maintenance alone takes 1–2% of the home's value every year.
- **Down payment:** Putting 20% down avoids private mortgage insurance.
- **Check the numbers:** Run a rent-versus-own calculator, then compare its results with how likely you are to move for work.
- **Priorities:** Treat a home as shelter first and an investment second. Put the roof before the return.
- **Renters can keep up:** Renters who steadily invest the money they save by not buying often end up with a net worth similar to owners'.
